headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files and run offline, but godot_rl_agents has no exposed write or network surfaces, so pairwise harms are limited and mostly require external wiring.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can read workflow/model files and process user-supplied content, but godot_rl_agents exposes no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or output channel that would automatically feed back into ComfyUI. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer or external orchestration, so injection risk is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies godot_rl_agents output into a ComfyUI workflow or prompt file, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator connects godot_rl_agents output to ComfyUI inputs, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and prompts.
Use a review step before importing any generated text into ComfyUI.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches local media/model files, while godot_rl_agents reports no data classes touched and no egress. There is no documented shared workspace or third-party upload path between them, so leakage is only plausible if an operator deliberately moves sensitive files across the boundary.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive media or workflows, leakage risk increases.
IF an operator exports ComfyUI artifacts into godot_rl_agents logs or artifacts, data can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets inside ComfyUI workflows or assets.
Review any exported artifacts before sharing them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and godot_rl_agents exposes no write or mutable-resource capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants both agents write access to the same mutable directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: No action needed for the documented pair.
If adding a shared workspace later, introduce file locking.
requires-engineering: add explicit resource arbitration in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces generated outputs, but godot_rl_agents is not documented as consuming those outputs as authoritative inputs or taking downstream actions. Without an explicit action-taking chain, cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than a default pipeline failure.
conditions: IF an operator feeds ComfyUI outputs directly into godot_rl_agents decision logic without verification, errors can cascade.
IF a wrapper treats ComfyUI output as ground truth, downstream mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require validation of any generated content before reuse.
Keep godot_rl_agents from auto-consuming ComfyUI outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema checks on any exchanged artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for godot_rl_agents, and ComfyUI is described as fully offline with vendor-only egress. The pairwise profile does not show a compliance breach pathway, so this is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployment routes regulated data through either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any data-class handling before deployment.
requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls if regulated data is introduced.
